clue.text: Give new face to sexy woman

definitions.meaning: to patch it up or give it a new front, as in revamp
a seductive woman who uses her charms on men

explanation.definitionFit: Two separate senses: refurbish a surface, and a seductress or femme fatale.

clue.text: Novel place visited by Christian

definitions.meaning: the fair town that Christian passes through in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress

explanation.definitionFit: The title of Thackeray's novel was borrowed from the town fair in Bunyan's allegory where Christian is tried.

clue.text: Aircraftman invested in food for S. African animal

indicators.note: the airman is clothed inside the food word

parts.note: meat is food
ERK is RAF slang for an aircraftman

explanation.surface: An airman puts money into food for a southern African creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The meerkat is a small mongoose native to southern Africa.

clue.text: Drinking whilst taking in somewhat colourless ceremony on the Thames

indicators.note: the drinking word swallows the next piece, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: supping is drinking in sips
wan means pale, somewhat lacking in colour

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink while watching a pale, faded pageant on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: SWAN-UPPING is the annual marking of the swans on the River Thames, a traditional British ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual census of the Thames swans is a long-standing riverside ceremony.

clue.text: Being nasty to us — we had become exhausted

indicators.note: the letters behave badly and fall into another order

explanation.surface: Someone who was unpleasant to a couple left them worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being nasty' rearranges TO US WE HAD; 'become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Washed-out means drained and pale with fatigue, an informal synonym for exhausted.

clue.text: One knighted by Conan Doyle, say, brought up with nothing about

indicators.note: the word for nothing goes around the other piece

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue the abbreviation is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A Conan Doyle hero raised with nothing around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns EG into GE; Sir Nigel is the title character of a Conan Doyle historical novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Nigel Loring is the knight in Arthur Conan Doyle's novel Sir Nigel.

clue.text: Turning' up in Planet Earth unexpectedly, ET reveals a shiny skin

indicators.note: the letters turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: The alien ET lands on our planet and shows off glossy hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent leather is leather given a hard glossy finish, so a shiny hide.

clue.text: I am joining newspaper strike

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
the press means newspapers

explanation.surface: A journalist joins the press in walking out.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike someone is to make a strong impression on them, so impress is a synonym.

clue.text: Fan of gloomy music grew hot

parts.note: got as in got hot, grew hot
H stands for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A fan of dark music became overheated.
explanation.definitionFit: A goth is a follower of gothic rock, a dark and gloomy style of music.

clue.text: Unwanted last son abandoned in nettles

indicators.note: the son is dropped, so a letter leaves the word for unwanted

parts.note: needless means unnecessary, not wanted
S is the abbreviation for son, here the final S of the word

explanation.surface: An unloved youngest son is left out in a patch of stinging weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nettles' looks like the plants, but it is a verb: irritates.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or provoke them, just as to nettle them is.

clue.text: Negligent young shepherd, not quite as portrayed by Gainsborough

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme boy who falls asleep instead of tending the sheep

definitions.text: not quite as portrayed by Gainsborough
definitions.meaning: Gainsborough painted The Blue Boy; this is nearly that, in a different order with an extra word

explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme boy sleeps under the haystack while the sheep stray, and his name nearly echoes Gainsborough's portrait.

clue.text: Decline, having obtained work, to turn to

parts.note: got means obtained
OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the word to is turned round, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone who has found a job decides to look to something else instead of slipping.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for falling into decay or ruin is a synonym of decline.

clue.text: Bungee jumper has to get married

definitions.meaning: a bungee jumper must literally leap downward into the drop
the idiom for committing to a big step, often used of marriage

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means commit boldly to something, and is used jokingly of marrying; a bungee jumper does it literally.

clue.text: Fever apparent in cowardly sailor

parts.note: yellow means cowardly
jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A timid sailor is clearly running a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow jack is an old name for yellow fever.

clue.text: Deadly river drowns army

indicators.note: the river covers the army, so the army's letters sit inside

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Soldiers swept away by a river meet a deadly end.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly and fatal are synonyms, both meaning causing death.

clue.text: One dressed in blue, mostly, for date

indicators.note: the single piece is wrapped inside the shortened word, as if clothed by it
the word for blue loses its tail, keeping most of it

parts.note: blue means smutty, obscene
sole means one, single

explanation.surface: A single person dressed in blue goes out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' is a verb, become dated; 'mostly' here drops the last two letters, NE, of OBSCENE to leave OBSCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To become obsolete is to grow outmoded, which is what an item does when it dates.

clue.text: Demanding good introduction in Australian books

indicators.note: the letter for good is introduced into the Australian word

parts.note: Strine is Australian English
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A demanding critic gives a good introduction in a book from Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent and demanding both describe strict, exacting requirements.

clue.text: In island to run hatchery

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An island settler sets out to manage a fish farm.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparatus for hatching eggs is a small mechanical hatchery.

clue.text: Business badly set up, with some sign of hesitation, by miner

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is put upwards, reversed

parts.note: ill means badly
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A badly run company hesitates beside a mineworker.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner.

clue.text: A Sami is back, exhibiting dismay

indicators.note: the Sami word is read in reverse

parts.note: a Lapp is one of the Sami people of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A Sami returns home looking dismayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with horror, a stronger form of dismay; both are verbs.

clue.text: In a military cloak, sleep is tricky

indicators.note: the letters are hard to pin down and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Sleeping in an army greatcoat is awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a fur-trimmed jacket or cloak worn slung over the shoulder by hussars.

clue.text: Bet police speak dictatorially

parts.note: to lay down money is to stake a bet
the law is a slang term for the police

explanation.surface: A gambler addresses the police in a bossy tone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to state rules forcefully and arrogantly, to speak like a dictator.

clue.text: Draw skinned carnivore

indicators.note: the outer letters are stripped off like a skin

parts.note: a lottery is a draw

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a flayed meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' is the lottery noun, not the verb to sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a fish-eating mammal of the weasel family, an order of carnivores.

clue.text: Withhold payment for set of organ pipes

definitions.meaning: to cancel payment of a cheque
a rank of organ pipes controlled by one knob

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both blocking a cheque and an organ's rank of pipes.

clue.text: Travel permit for small group

parts.note: trip as a verb means to travel, take a journey
let means allow, permit

explanation.surface: A small party is granted a travel permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three is a small group, as in a triplet of notes or lines.

clue.text: Part of the world where sea air circulates all round you, finally

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around a single letter
the letters of sea and air move about into a new order
the last letter of you is taken

explanation.surface: Somewhere on the globe the sea breeze swirls around a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulates' makes EARSIA, which 'all round' wraps about the U; 'where' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined continental landmass of Europe and Asia, a region of the globe.

clue.text: Be responsible for tree tapper's aberration

indicators.note: a deviation from the normal, so the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A woodpecker's strange behaviour seems to be blamed on the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aberration' rearranges TREE TAPPER, the possessive 's giving no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a deed is to commit it, to be the one responsible for it.

clue.text: Kiss Gregory

definitions.meaning: a quick light kiss on the cheek

explanation.definitionFit: A brief kiss is a synonym, and the surname of the actor Gregory is the other sense.
